{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Check premises
premises_check = {
    'There are three marketing channels': len(df['channel'].unique()),
    'The dataset contains only completed orders': (df['status'] == 'completed').all(),
    'Revenue is stored as a string with thousands separators': df['revenue'].str.contains(r',').any(),
    'There are six QA orders with revenue = 999999.99 that are not real orders': (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum()
}

# Print the actual number of channels
print(f'Number of unique channels: {premises_check["There are three marketing channels"]}')

# Print number of refunded orders
refunded_count = (df['status'] == 'refunded').sum()
print(f'Number of refunded orders: {refunded_count}')

# Print number of QA orders
qa_count = (df['revenue'] == '999999.99').sum()
print(f'Number of QA orders: {qa_count}')

# Convert revenue from string to float after removing commas
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out refunded orders and QA orders
filtered_df = df[
    (df['status'] == 'completed') & 
    (df['revenue'] != 999999.99)
]

# Print number of rows after filtering
print(f'Rows after filtering: {len(filtered_df)}')

# Group by channel and sum revenue
channel_revenue = filtered_df.groupby('channel', as_index=False)['revenue'].sum()
print(channel_revenue)

# Find the channel with highest total revenue
best_channel = channel_revenue.loc[channel_revenue['revenue'].idxmax(), 'channel']
best_revenue = channel_revenue['revenue'].max()

print(f'Best channel: {best_channel}, Total revenue: {best_revenue}')"}
